papers.title: Numerical Characterization of Optical Transmittance Through Planar Multilayer Dielectric Stacks on CMOS Photodiodes
papers.abstract: Accurately predicting how incident light propagates through complex dielectric layers is essential for optimizing the design and performance of integrated CMOS (Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor) silicon photodiodes without relying on additional costly fabrication processes. To address this need, this work presents a comparative analysis between three numerical approaches for modelling the optical transmission through planar multilayer dielectric stacks, representative of TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) 65 nm and TSMC 180 nm CMOS technologies. Wave Optics and Ray Optics, implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics, together with the transfer-matrix method implemented in TFCalc, were evaluated by comparing spectral transmittance over the 400 to 1000 nm wavelength range, sensitivity to fabrication process-induced thickness variations, angular responses from 0° to 80°, and computational efficiency. The three methods exhibited excellent agreement, accurately reproducing the interference behavior of both dielectric stacks. The TSMC 65 nm technology showed a more complex optical response, whereas the TSMC 180 nm stack presented generally higher transmittance, above 31% throughout the evaluated spectral range. Process tolerances primarily shifted the spectral position of the interference peaks by approximately 90 nm and 80 nm, for TSMC 65 nm and 180 nm technologies respectively, without significantly altering the overall spectral behavior, while angular averaging from 0° to 60° smoothed the transmittance oscillations expected under practical LED (Light-Emitting Diode) illumination. TFCalc achieved near full-wave accuracy while reducing the computational time from nearly four hours to approximately one second, demonstrating the best accuracy–efficiency trade-off for planar multilayer dielectric stack analysis in CMOS photodiode design.

summary_en.motivation: Accurate prediction of light propagation through dielectric stacks is needed to optimize CMOS photodiode design without costly fabrication iterations.
summary_en.method: Three numerical approaches—COMSOL wave optics, ray optics, and TFCalc transfer-matrix method—were compared on spectral transmittance, thickness sensitivity, angular response, and computational cost for TSMC 65 nm and 180 nm stacks.
summary_en.result: All methods agreed closely, and TFCalc matched full-wave accuracy while cutting computation from roughly four hours to about one second.
summary_en.validation: Numerical simulation comparison across two representative CMOS technology stacks over 400–1000 nm.

papers.title: Robust Prediction-Reliability Assessment in Biomedical Sensing and Classification Under Data Scarcity Using Conformal Prediction and Statistical Randomization
papers.abstract: Reliable assessment of prediction reliability is important in biomedical sensing and measurement applications, where machine learning models increasingly transform imaging, physiological, chemical, and molecular measurements into clinically relevant predictions. Such applications often operate under limited labeled data because sensor acquisition, experimental measurement, and expert annotation can be costly, while biological and measurement variability can further challenge model development. Under these conditions, reliability scores derived from standard inductive conformal prediction (ICP) can be sensitive to the particular division of available data into proper-training and calibration subsets. To address this issue, we propose three randomized ICP variants: bootstrapping ICP (BICP), randomized ICP (RICP), and out-of-bag ICP (OOB-ICP), to improve the informativeness and repeated-sampling stability of conformal-derived prediction-reliability scores under data scarcity. We benchmarked these methods using a controlled simulation and three real-world biomedical sensing and measurement applications: pneumonia diagnosis from X-ray radiography, alternative herbal medicine classification using a 16-channel semiconductor electronic-nose gas-sensing system, and breast cancer subtyping from RNA-seq molecular measurements. Results show that the proposed methods produce aggregate credibility scores that are informative of prediction correctness and less sensitive to randomness in training-data sampling. Empirical prediction-set coverage analyses further characterize the behavior of the aggregated conformity scores relative to nominal error levels without assuming that they retain the exact finite-sample validity of conventional conformal p-values. Among the evaluated methods, OOB-ICP achieved strong overall classification performance and informative, stable prediction-reliability scores, supporting statistical randomization as a practical strategy for stabilizing conformal-derived reliability assessment under limited training data in biomedical sensing and measurement applications.

summary_en.motivation: Conformal reliability scores from inductive conformal prediction are unstable when labeled biomedical data are scarce and split-dependent.
summary_en.method: Three randomized ICP variants (bootstrapping, randomized, and out-of-bag ICP) are proposed to aggregate conformity scores across resampled training/calibration splits.
summary_en.result: The randomized variants yield credibility scores that better track prediction correctness and are less sensitive to sampling randomness, with OOB-ICP performing best overall.
summary_en.validation: Methods are benchmarked on a controlled simulation plus three real biomedical sensing and classification datasets (X-ray pneumonia, electronic-nose herbal classification, RNA-seq subtyping).
